name: Selank

card.summary: A Russian-developed anxiolytic peptide that forum users group with Semax as a nootropic; human evidence is limited to a few Russian-language studies.
card.note: Approved only in Russia; products sold elsewhere are unregulated research chemicals.

quick.overview:
Selank is a synthetic seven-amino-acid peptide derived from tuftsin, developed in Russia and registered there as nasal drops for anxiety. On looksmax.org it is discussed alongside Semax and Cerebrolysin as a nootropic, with members asking whether such peptides are "cope".

It has no connection to physical appearance; its place in the community is as a cognition and mood supplement. Published research is mostly animal and in-vitro work, much of it from Russian groups.
quick.mechanism: Studies in cells and animals suggest it may influence GABA-related gene expression and inhibit enkephalin-degrading enzymes, which researchers propose as routes to its anxiolytic effects.
quick.risks: It is a registered drug only in Russia. Outside Russia it is sold as a research chemical without regulatory oversight. A 2021 pharmacology review grouped it among agents acting on GABA receptors.

lead: Selank is a synthetic seven-amino-acid peptide (Thr-Lys-Pro-Arg-Pro-Gly-Pro) built as a longer-lasting analog of tuftsin, a natural fragment of immunoglobulin G. It was developed at the Institute of Molecular Genetics of the Russian Academy of Sciences together with the Zakusov Institute of Pharmacology, and is used in Russia as an intranasal anxiolytic. [1][15]

People who take an interest in it for appearance reasons usually do so through an indirect chain: calmer mood and lower stress, steadier focus and sleep, and from there the confidence and routine consistency that looks-related effort depends on. The compound itself has no reported direct effect on skin, bone or body composition. [1][8]

Published work includes small Russian clinical trials in anxiety disorders that compared it with benzodiazepine-type drugs, a resting-state fMRI study in healthy volunteers, and animal and cell experiments on enkephalin-degrading enzymes, GABAergic gene expression and stress behaviour. [17][18][19][20][5][21] Within looksmaxxing forums it is discussed as a nootropic, usually next to Semax and Cerebrolysin. [12][13][14]

paras: Selank came out of the Russian peptide-drug programme at the Institute of Molecular Genetics, in collaboration with the Zakusov Institute of Pharmacology. Tuftsin, the Thr-Lys-Pro-Arg fragment of the IgG heavy chain, is broken down quickly in the body, so the designers added a Pro-Gly-Pro tail to make a more stable seven-residue analog with anxiolytic and nootropic properties. [1][22] Reference works name Ashmarin and Myasoedov as leading researchers on the project. [1]

The same institute developed Semax, a heptapeptide analog of an ACTH fragment first described in the literature in 1991 and used in Russia for stroke and cognitive disorders; Selank and Semax are often mentioned together. [16] Both are available in Russian and Ukrainian pharmacies, according to Wikipedia. [15]

In vitro work reported that Selank and Semax inhibit enkephalin-degrading enzymes in human serum, which authors proposed as a possible basis of its anxiolytic activity. [5][6] Studies in cell cultures and in rats have found altered expression of genes involved in GABAergic neurotransmission, and reviews describe additional effects on monoamine metabolism, brain-derived neurotrophic factor and cytokine signalling. [7][21][8][15]

Glyproline peptides, which contain proline-glycine-proline motifs, have been described as unusually stable among regulatory peptides, and Selank has been studied with them. [2][9] A 2021 pharmacology review grouped Selank among agents acting on GABA receptors. [3] A 2021 rat study examined cytokine levels under social stress. [23]

Trials and Russian practice use intranasal drops. Wikipedia lists nasal and intravenous routes, and describes the lyophilised peptide as refrigerated once dissolved. [15] Outside Russia, vendors sell it as a research peptide. [1]

A 2008 comparative trial in 62 patients with generalized anxiety disorder and neurasthenia compared Selank (30 patients) with medazepam (32). The anxiolytic effects were similar, and Selank additionally showed antiasthenic and psychostimulant effects; enkephalin activity in serum was also measured. [17]

A 2014 study in 60 patients with phobic-anxiety and somatoform disorders compared Selank with phenazepam and reported a pronounced anxiolytic and mild nootropic effect that lasted a week after the last dose. [18] A 2015 randomised trial compared phenazepam alone (30 patients) with Selank plus phenazepam (40); the combination reached its effect earlier on a depression scale and reduced the tranquilizer's side effects such as attention and memory impairment and sedation. [19]

A 2020 resting-state fMRI study in 52 healthy participants examined how Selank and Semax change whole-brain connectivity of the amygdala and dorsolateral prefrontal cortex. [20] Most trials are small and come from Russian groups; no published trial has tested Selank for an appearance outcome.

Rodent experiments of tuftsin-family peptides under conflict-stress conditions reported anti-stress behavioural effects, and a rat study reported that Selank enhanced diazepam's anxiety-reducing effect under chronic mild stress. [4][11] Other rat studies cover liver morphology under chronic foot-shock stress and signs of morphine withdrawal. [25][24] A 2026 review of therapeutic peptides in orthopaedics lists Selank among neuroactive peptides and notes that clinical trials are currently lacking. [26]

Looksmax.org threads ask how Selank differs from Semax, whether Semax, Selank and Cerebrolysin are 'cope', and how safe it is to take one or both. [12][13][14][27] Replies are often joking or terse, and members describe themselves as unfamiliar with the compounds. A T Nation member asked in 2016 whether anyone had tried it alongside TRT and growth-hormone secretagogues. [28]

Selank is a prescription drug in Russia, reported as registered in 2009, and is unapproved for human therapeutic use in most other countries. [1][15] Wikipedia describes it as generally unscheduled; outside Russia it is sold as a research chemical without regulatory oversight. [15][1]

lore.intro: Selank appears on looksmax.org mainly in questions about Semax and nootropics rather than as an appearance compound [12][13].

claims.claim: Selank and Semax are useful nootropics for focus and mood.
claims.believers: Some members ask for experiences with the pair and for guidance on when to use each [12][13].
claims.experts: Published research is largely animal and cell studies, many from Russian groups [10][11][7].

claims.believers: Other members dismiss them as cope, while the original poster in one thread says replies were mostly trolling [13][14].
claims.experts: No published studies have tested them against looksmaxxing goals.

claims.believers: Proponents point to Russian reports that it lowers anxiety while leaving alertness intact, and some forum members ask for personal experiences with it. [1][12]
claims.experts: Small Russian trials report anxiolytic effects similar to medazepam and phenazepam, with fewer cognitive side effects in the add-on study; the trials are small and local. [17][18][19]

claims.claim: Selank is safe to take alongside other stacks.
claims.believers: Forum users ask about safety and combining it with Semax or with TRT and secretagogues. [27][28]
claims.experts: No large safety dataset exists outside Russian trials, and outside Russia products are unregulated research chemicals. [15][26]

angle.text: Selank is taken for its anxiety-reducing and cognitive effects rather than any direct change to how the body looks. Users who mention it place it among mood and focus aids that may make it easier to keep up training, skincare and social confidence.
